messages:
Sam (docs): Pinging folks. I opened a PR to add a compact "evidence package" guide for SOC2 reviewers that covers staging exports to S3, the consent ledger format, and a short SQL export example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2629 :wave:

Ivy (security): Nice. Two must-haves: explicit default redaction keys (ip_address, user_email, api_key, auth_token, location) and a prescriptive integrity check (sha256 in metadata).

Ken (infra): For S3 staging docs, call out a presigned URL flow and that the package is encrypted server-side with AES-256. Example (curl):

```bash
curl -X PUT "${PRESIGNED_URL}" -H "x-checksum:sha256:${CHECKSUM}" --upload-file export-package.tar.gz
```

Marta (legal): For any "full-export" opt-in we need a consent ledger entry recorded server-side: consent_id, consent_ts, requester_email, approval_ticket. Also add text that legal holds supersede retention rules and are recorded as legal_hold_id in export metadata.

Sam (docs): I'll add both. Thinking to include a tiny machine-readable consent snippet in the package metadata:

```json
{"consent_id":"cons_2026_01_09_01","consent_ts":"2026-01-09T15:12:03Z","requester":"alice@example.com","approval_ticket":"SUP-1122"}
```

Jo (devex): Can we also include an example SQL query for auditors who want a human-readable sample of how to pull an event set? Something like:```
SELECT ts, actor_type, actor_id, action, resource FROM audit_events WHERE ts BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-10-31' AND tenant_id = 't_987';
```

Ivy (security): Add a short note: "server-side redaction is authoritative; do not rely on client-side redaction." Also recommend storing per-export sha256 in metadata and a copy in an audit index for cross-checking.

Ken (infra): Implementation detail: our export worker stages files to a private S3 bucket under `s3://redwood-exports/<tenant>/<export_id>/` then generates presigned URLs with a 24h expiration. I'll add that path and the 24h TTL to the doc.

Marta (legal): Add guidance for regional retention: hosted default 90 days, dedicated contractual, private operator-defined. Also include a sample retention policy JSON and mention retention dispute workflow (request -> legal review -> consent recorded -> rule applied).

Sam (docs): Draft now includes: 1) S3 staging flow with presigned PUT/GET examples; 2) consent ledger JSON sample; 3) SQL auditor query; 4) redaction checklist; 5) example of export metadata with checksum and legal_hold_id.

Jo (devex): For SDKs, add a Python snippet that lists available export packages and shows how to download with streaming and verify checksum. Keep it short.

Sam (docs): I'll add a minimal python snippet and a one-line curl example for auditors. Also adding a tiny migration note for consumer-facing field change: `user_id` integer -> `actor.id` string-prefixed (e.g., "user:u_42").

Ivy (security): One more: include a short paragraph about verifying integrity after download: compute sha256 and compare to metadata, and for extra rigor, show the header name we use in presigned upload (`x-checksum`).

Marta (legal): Looks good. Add explicit retention of consent records per region and a link to audit export policy for legal reviewers.

CI-bot: docs/pr-2629  checks passed, linkcheck ok :white_check_mark:

Sam (docs): Thanks everyone — I'll fold these edits in and request final approvals from Ivy & Marta before merging tomorrow morning. :coffee:
